events.title: Strait of Hormuz disrupted; shipping halted and oil prices surge
events.summary: The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of global oil passes daily, became functionally disrupted as the IRGC broadcast warnings that passage was not allowed. More than 200 vessels including oil tankers and liquefied gas carriers anchored in and around the strait. Major tanker owners, oil and gas majors, and trading houses suspended shipments. Japan's three largest shipping companies—Nippon Yusen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, and Kawasaki Kisen—halted operations through the strait. Container lines diverted away from highest-risk corridors. War-risk insurance costs for tankers jumped 25 to 50 percent. Brent crude surged roughly 8% on open with spikes around 10% reported in the immediate reaction window. S&P Global Platts began reviewing deliverability and pricing mechanics for Middle East crude. Analysts warned prices could reach $100 or more if disruption persists. The UAE Capital Markets Authority ordered both stock exchanges closed March 2–3.
